p: wise men: Which are esteemed wise by the world.
judgment: Let us examine the matter uprightly.
away my judgment: That is, has afflicted me without measure.
right: Should I say, I am wicked, being an innocent?
incurable without transgression: I am more punished, than my sin deserves.
scorning like water: Which is compelled to receive your reproach and scorns of many for his foolish words.
company with the workers of iniquity: Meaning that Job was like the wicked, because he seemed not to glorify God and submit himself to his judgments.
It profiteth a man nothing that: He wrests Job's words who said that God's children are often punished in this world, and the wicked go free.
delight himself with God: That is, live godly, Ge 5:22.
he set his heart upon man: To destroy him.
and his breath: The breath of life which he gave man.
govern: If God were not just, how could be govern the world?
wicked: If man by nature fears to speak evil of such as have power, then they should be much more afraid to speak evil of God.
and the people shall be troubled: When they look not for it.
and pass away: The messengers of visitation that God will send.
enter into judgment with God: God does not afflict man above measure so that he should have opportunity to contend with him.
number: For all his creatures are at hand to serve him, so that he needs not to seek for any other army.
works: Make it known that they are wicked.
night: Declare the things that were hid.
others: Meaning, openly in the sight of all men.
come unto him: By their cruelty and extortion.

hypocrite reign not: When tyrants sit in the throne of justice which under pretence of executing justice are hypocrites and oppress the people, it is a sign that God has drawn back his countenance of favour from that place.
to be said unto God: It only belongs to God to moderate his corrections, and not to man.
That which I see not teach: Thus Elihu speaks in the person of God, as it were mocking Job, because he would be wiser than God.
thy mind: Will God use your counsel in doing his works?
it: Thus he speaks in the person of God, as though Job should chose and refuse affliction at his pleasure.
tried unto the end because of: That he may speak as much as he can, that we may answer him and all the wicked that will use such arguments.
addeth rebellion unto his sin: He stands stubbornly to the maintenance of his cause.
